chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When two Witr prayers gather upon you, or three, or more than that, then fulfill them as they have been missed, distinguishing between every two Witr prayers with one Salat, because the Witr is the last one; do not precede anything before its first one, the first is the first. So begin with the first when you fulfill the Salat of your night, then the Witr.
He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Two Witr prayers cannot be in one night except that one of the two is a Qada (make-up) prayer.'

And he said: 'If you pray Witr at the beginning of the night and stand (to pray) at the end of the night, then your first Witr is a Qada, and whatever you prayed from the Salat during your entire night, let it be Qada until the end of your Salat, for these are for your night, and let the last of your Salats be the Witr, the Witr of your night.'

key_terms.قَضَاء: Qada (make-up prayer for missed obligatory or recommended acts)

ai.seo_question: How should one make up multiple missed Witr prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the procedural hierarchy for Qada (making up) Witr prayers, establishing that the first Witr offered becomes the Qada for any subsequent night's obligation, thereby ensuring the Witr remains the definitive conclusion of the night's worship. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that Witr is an integral part of the night prayer structure rather than a standalone optional act, requiring strict sequential fulfillment to maintain spiritual order. The emphasis on concluding with Witr reflects the theological significance of sealing one's night devotion with the Prophet's prescribed final prayer.
